name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 10-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Sara Jacobs running with a large fundraising advantage and no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Jacobs near 96% to win
No public general-election polling, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 district, incumbency, a clear money edge, and no outside spending against her, while markets price her around 96%. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, a Safe D forecast stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Republican Ricardo Cabrera within single digits, or significant outside spending against Jacobs, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She advanced to the general election against Republican Ricardo Cabrera, a challenger with no reported fundraising or outside support. Jacobs has raised roughly $1.6 million and faces no recorded outside spending against her.

With no public general-election polling and no expert ratings on the race, the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Jacobs heavily. Prediction markets put her chances near 96 percent, consistent with a comfortable expected margin in the low twenties.
